questionText:
Match the models of secularism in List I with their defining principles in List II:

List I:
(A) Western (Wall of Separation)
(B) French Laïcité
(C) Indian Secularism
(D) Sarva Dharma Sambhava

List II:
(I) Equal respect for all religious faiths and spiritual traditions
(II) Strict prohibition of all visible religious symbols in public civic institutions and schools
(III) Complete mutual non-interference: state has no religious role and religion has no state role
(IV) Principled distance allowing non-discriminatory state intervention for social justice and reform

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Wall of separation is mutual non-interference; Laïcité bans visible symbols; Indian is principled distance; Sarva Dharma Sambhava is equal respect.
Hence, Option B is correct.
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.

chapter: The Challenges of Unity in Diversity
questionText:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions based on the
passage:
 
The background to the SRC is as follows. In the 1920s, the Indian National
Congress was reconstituted on linguistic lines. Its provincial units now
followed the logic of language – one for Marathi speakers, another for
Oriya speakers, etc. At the same time, Gandhi and other leaders promised
their followers that when freedom came, the new nation would be based on
a new set of provinces based on the principle of language. However, when
India was finally freed in 1947, it was also divided. Now, when the
proponents of linguistic states asked for this promise to be redeemed, the
Congress hesitated. Partition was the consequence of intense attachment
to one’s faith; how many more partitions would that other intense loyalty,
language, lead to?
 
 
 
When was the Report of the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC)
implemented?

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
The States Reorganisation Act 1956 reorganized state boundaries on linguistic grounds, creating 14 states and 6 union territories, which stabilized India's federal structure.
Hence, option (A) is correct.

questionText: Which of the following statements regarding Sri Lanka's Failure of Nation-State Model in The Challenges of Unity in Diversity is INCORRECT / NOT true?

options.text: It conforms strictly to the standard equilibrium conditions defined in NCERT The Challenges of Unity in Diversity.

options.text: It operates in direct violation of the fundamental conservation laws of The Challenges of Unity in Diversity.

detailedSolution:

According to standard NCERT The Challenges of Unity in Diversity specifications, Sri Lanka's Failure of Nation-State Model is fully consistent with established principles and does not violate conservation laws.
